description: The annualised value of all active subscription contracts. The primary top-line SaaS metric at Acme. Calculated as MRR × 12. Excludes one-time order revenue.
The monthly normalised value of an active subscription. Source of truth is subscriptions.mrr_usd. Summed across active subscriptions to derive total company MRR.

A recurring-revenue contract between Acme and a customer for a specific product and plan. The subscriptions table is the source of truth for all MRR/ARR figures. A subscription has a billing cycle (monthly or annual), a seat count, and a status (active, cancelled, past_due, trialing).
A subscription that has been cancelled, resulting in a reduction of ARR. Identified by subscriptions.status = 'cancelled' and a non-null subscriptions.cancelled_date.
The date on which a subscription is next due for renewal. Used by CSMs to prioritise at-risk accounts and by finance for ARR forecasting.
The cadence at which a subscription is billed — either monthly or annual. Annual billing typically carries a discount and improves cash collection.
A one-time, non-recurring purchase — typically professional services, training, or a perpetual license. Distinct from a subscription. Revenue is recognised at delivery rather than ratably.
The total USD value of delivered or completed one-time orders in a period. Derived from orders.total_usd where status not in ('cancelled', 'returned').
A formal billing document issued to a customer against an order or subscription. Tracks amount due, due date, and payment status. An invoice can be linked to a subscription, an order, or both.
An invoice that has been sent to the customer but not yet paid. Identified by invoices.status = 'sent' or 'overdue'. Key indicator of cash collection risk.
A cash receipt applied against an invoice. Tracks payment method, amount, and processing status.
The number of user licences purchased under a subscription. Used for seat-based pricing and expansion tracking.
The named tier or package of a subscription (e.g. Enterprise Tier 3, Cloud Growth). Determines feature entitlements and pricing.
A qualified sales deal being pursued with a customer or prospect. The core pipeline and forecast record. Each opportunity has a stage, expected value, probability, and expected close date.
The current position of a deal in the sales process: discovery → proposal → negotiation → closed_won / closed_lost.
The expected total contract value of an opportunity in USD, as assessed by the account executive.
The estimated likelihood (0.0–1.0) that an open opportunity will close as won. Multiplied by deal amount to produce weighted pipeline.
A risk-adjusted view of open pipeline calculated as opportunity amount × win probability. Used for revenue forecasting.
An opportunity that has been successfully closed as a new booking. Identified by opportunities.stage = 'closed_won'.
The total value of new contracts signed in a period. Derived from closed_won opportunities. Distinct from revenue, which is recognised over the subscription term.
Free-text explanation of why a deal was lost. Populated only on closed_lost opportunities. Used for competitive and win/loss analysis.
A formal price proposal generated against an opportunity. Quotes are versioned; the highest-version accepted quote represents the final agreed deal terms.
The percentage reduction applied from list price on a quote. Tracked per quote for margin and pricing governance analysis.
A logged touchpoint in the sales process — call, email, meeting, or demo. Linked to an opportunity, lead, or contact. Used to measure rep engagement and pipeline velocity.
The Acme sales representative who owns a deal or customer account. Referenced as owner_employee_id on opportunities and account_owner_id on customers.
The expected or actual date a deal closes. Used as the partition key on the opportunities table and is the basis for quarterly pipeline reporting.
A B2B company that has purchased or is being sold to. The customers table is the source of truth for account ownership, segmentation, and lifetime value. One row per company.
The sales tier a customer belongs to: enterprise, mid_market, or smb. Drives coverage model, pricing, and support SLAs.
The cumulative revenue collected from a customer from first contract to date. Stored as customers.lifetime_value_usd.
The date a customer signed their first contract with Acme. Stored as customers.acquired_date. Used for cohort analysis and tenure calculations.
A 0–100 composite score computed by the Customer Success model to indicate account risk. Low scores flag at-risk renewals.
The current lifecycle state of a customer account: active, churned, or prospect.
An individual person at a customer account. A customer may have many contacts. is_primary identifies the main point of contact; is_decision_maker flags economic buyers.
A customer contact who holds economic buying authority. Identified by customer_contacts.is_decision_maker = TRUE.
The Acme employee responsible for post-sale customer health and renewals. Referenced as owner_employee_id on subscriptions.
A top-of-funnel prospect that has not yet been qualified into an opportunity. Captured with source, score, and status. Converts to a customer via converted_customer_id.
The channel through which a lead was acquired: web, event, referral, outbound, ads, or social.
A 0–100 score from the marketing automation platform indicating a lead's engagement and fit. Higher scores are prioritised for SDR outreach.
The event where a qualified lead becomes a new customer account. Tracked via leads.converted_customer_id and leads.converted_at.
A marketing initiative designed to generate leads or pipeline, run across a specific channel (email, event, paid search, etc.) with a defined budget and duration.
The medium through which a campaign reaches its audience: email, social, paid_search, event, content, or ads.
The planned spend allocated to a marketing campaign. Compared against campaigns.spend_usd to track over/under-spend.
A digital interaction captured from the Acme website, such as a page view, form fill, or content download. Linked to a customer or anonymous session.

A sellable software product or service in Acme's catalogue, including on-premise and SaaS offerings, professional services, and training. The products table tracks list price, cost, and active/retired status.
The standard undiscounted price for a product before any negotiated discount is applied.
The internal unit cost of delivering a product, used for gross margin calculations.
A grouping of related products used for reporting and catalogue organisation.
A single product line within an order, capturing quantity and unit price. Multiple line items compose an order.
A customer-reported issue or request tracked through resolution. Classified by priority (low, normal, high, urgent) and category (billing, technical, bug, feature_request).
The elapsed time between a support ticket being created and the first agent response. A key SLA metric. Derived from support_tickets.first_response_at − support_tickets.created_at.
The total time from ticket creation to resolution. Derived from support_tickets.resolved_at − support_tickets.created_at.
Customer Satisfaction score (1–5) collected after ticket resolution. NULL if the customer did not respond to the survey.
The urgency level of a support ticket: low, normal, high, or urgent. Drives SLA response targets.
A message or note added to a support ticket by an agent or customer after initial creation. Tracked in ticket_comments.
An individual who works at Acme, past or present. The employees table stores the current role snapshot; employee_role_history provides the time-series of all role changes.
The count of active employees at a point in time. Derived by filtering employees where employment_status = 'active'.
The date an employee started at Acme. Used for tenure calculations, onboarding cohort analysis, and anniversary reporting.
The length of time an employee has been at Acme, calculated from hire_date (or role start_date for role-specific tenure) to the current date or termination_date.
An organisational unit within Acme (e.g. Engineering, Sales, Customer Success). Employees and projects are grouped by department.
A canonical role title with an associated level code (IC1–IC8, M1–M5) and salary band. Prevents free-text title drift.
A standardised seniority code: IC1–IC8 for individual contributors, M1–M5 for managers. Drives salary banding and promotion eligibility.
The approved minimum and maximum base salary range for a given job title and level.

A point-in-time change to an employee's compensation package (new_hire, merit, promotion, or adjustment). The compensation table is a full history; the most recent row per employee represents the current package.
The annualised fixed cash component of an employee's total compensation.
The USD value of equity awarded to an employee at grant time. Tracked per compensation event.
A half-yearly formal assessment of an employee's performance, resulting in a categorical rating (exceeds, meets, below) and a numeric score (1.0–5.0).
A time-series record of every role an employee has held, including title, department, team, and manager. Used for promotion velocity, reorg, and tenure-in-role analysis.
An employee's request for leave (vacation, sick, parental, etc.) including approval status and date range.
A record of an employee completing a training course, including their final score and completion status.
A physical Acme office location worldwide. The offices table is the source of truth for employee work locations and regional headcount capacity planning.
An external supplier of goods or services to Acme. Vendors are linked to contracts that track annual spend commitments.
A procurement agreement with an external vendor specifying annual committed spend, term dates, and auto-renewal behaviour.
The committed or expected annual spend on a vendor contract in USD. Used by FP&A for operating expense planning.
An internal cross-functional initiative with a defined budget, lead, timeline, and status. The projects table tracks planned vs. actual spend for budget variance analysis.
The approved USD budget for an internal project. Compared against projects.spend_usd to identify over-runs.
An allocation of an employee to a project, specifying their role and the percentage of their time committed.
